facts.text: MAHLI Calibration Target was deployed at Gale Crater during Curiosity (MSL) in 2012.

Mounted on the rover's deck, the MAHLI calibration target includes a 1909 Lincoln penny (chosen for its fine detail), colour chips, a metric bar graphic, and a UV-fluorescent target. It is used to calibrate the Mars Hand Lens Imager. The penny belongs to principal investigator Ken Edgett — it is the only US coin on Mars.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Provides a known reference for colour, scale, and UV fluorescence so scientists can ensure MAHLI images are accurate across Mars's changing conditions.
The 1909 Lincoln penny on Mars is a beloved cultural artefact — the only U.S. coin on another planet, still riding on Curiosity's deck.
